quick.summary: Why saving data and doing math should not happen on the same server.
quick.takeaway: Keep storage cheap, and only spin up expensive processing power when you need it.

beats.line: The database is terribly slow every morning. Should we buy a bigger server?
Think of a heavy backpack. Do you wear it everywhere, or use a locker?
I use a locker. I only carry what I need.
Right. Storing things and doing work are different jobs. Separate them.
The industry calls this decoupling storage and compute.
Can I just say separating storage from processing?
Keep heavy data in cheap storage. Add processing power only when you need it.
So we add processing power for the morning rush, then turn it off.
And you never pay for a giant server to sit idle.

quiz.question: Why is separating storage from processing an advantage?
options: You can scale your computing power up and down without moving heavy data.
It allows everyone on the team to delete old records automatically.
It forces your database to read files much slower.
It automatically masks any sensitive customer records.
quiz.explanation: Separation means you only pay for big computing power when you are actively using it, while data rests in cheap storage.

quiz.question: Separating storage from processing usually makes it harder to scale during busy hours.
quiz.explanation: It actually makes it much easier to scale, because you can simply add processing power without touching the stored data.
